computation: Step 1: Aggregate claims = token_supply × claim_value_per_token = 100000000 × 1.00 = 100000000 EUR
Step 2: Aggregate reserve value = sum of marked-to-market reserve assets = 45000000 + 42000000 + 14000000 = 101000000 EUR
Step 4: Test against full-backing requirement: coverage_ratio >= 1.0 ?
article_basis: Article 36(7) MiCA (aggregate value of reserve of assets at least equal to aggregate value of claims)
tail_convention: Coverage is a higher-is-better metric; the adverse tail is the LOW tail. This case examines the realised point estimate (no stress); adverse outcomes are those driving coverage below 1.0.
weakest_point: Reliance on mark-to-market of the bond and liquid-asset sleeves; any simultaneous adverse price move not captured in the point estimate would erode the 1% buffer.

computation: Step 2: Component B (percentage of average reserve) = 0.02 × 250000000 = 5000000 EUR (non-significant)
Step 3: Component C (quarter of fixed overheads) = 0.25 × 1200000 = 300000 EUR
Step 4: Required own funds = max(A, B, C) = max(350000, 5000000, 300000) = 5000000 EUR

result.regulatory_verdict: adequate if actual CET1 own funds >= 5000000 EUR against Art 35(1) highest-of test; inadequate otherwise

article_basis: Article 35(1) MiCA (highest of EUR 350 000; 2% of average reserve of assets; quarter of fixed overheads); Article 45(5) raises the percentage to 3% for significant ARTs
tail_convention: Own-funds requirement is a lower-bound threshold (higher own funds better); adverse tail for the metric 'own-funds surplus' is the LOW tail. This case is a deterministic point calculation, not a stress distribution.
weakest_point: Average reserve is itself an estimate over six months of daily EOD values; any structural decline in reserve size after the averaging window immediately raises the effective percentage burden relative to current reserve.

result.regulatory_verdict: inadequate against full-backing test (Art 36) under the applied haircuts; baseline was adequate, stressed is not

article_basis: Article 36 (reserve value >= claims at all times, mark-to-market); stress testing obligations under Art 35(5) and liquidity management under Art 36/45
tail_convention: Coverage is higher-is-better; the adverse tail is the LOW tail. This case deliberately applies adverse (price-declining) haircuts and examines the resulting low coverage outcome.
weakest_point: The 15% haircut sleeve and the simultaneous application across correlated liquid assets; the residual buffer after stress is negative, leaving no margin for further adverse moves or redemption spikes.

computation: Step 1: Redemption obligation amount = tokens_presented × market_value_per_token = 5000000 × 1.00 = 5000000 EUR (payable in funds other than e-money, or by delivery of referenced assets)
Step 3: Post-redemption aggregate reserve (assuming exact matching decrease) = 101000000 - 5000000 = 96000000 EUR
Step 5: Issuer must ensure corresponding decrease in reserve assets (Art 36) and settle per the redemption policy (Art 39)

result.regulatory_verdict: adequate provided reserve is reduced commensurately and settlement occurs per Art 39 policy; obligation is permanent and must be met at market value of referenced assets

article_basis: Article 39 MiCA (permanent right of redemption at market value of referenced assets or by delivery; corresponding reserve adjustment under Art 36)
tail_convention: Post-redemption coverage remains higher-is-better; adverse tail is LOW coverage after the simultaneous reduction of reserve and claims. This case examines a matched par redemption (neutral to coverage ratio).
weakest_point: Liquidity of the reserve sleeves that must be monetised to fund the cash redemption; if the assets sold realise less than the mark used for the obligation, coverage erodes.
